headline: Implements the Debit Cards module for card issuance, lifecycle management, and payment authorisation.
summary: Adds the Cards module with API endpoints, CardService business logic, Card domain entity and events, database table, and DI registration. Customers can issue, freeze, unfreeze, and cancel their cards, while staff can authorise card payments against status, a 2000 per-transaction limit, and account funds via the ledger.
business: Customers gain debit card issuance and self-service freeze, unfreeze, and cancellation controls with masked card numbers in responses. Staff can authorise card payments up to a fixed 2000 limit per transaction, rounding amounts away from zero and moving authorised funds into a Suspense account.

reasons.text: Class-level Customer authorization policy blocks Staff access to Authorise endpoint
reasons.claim: CardsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level, while Authorise is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Staff)]. In ASP.NET Core, controller- and action-level authorization attributes are evaluated conjunctively (logical AND), so Authorise requires both Customer and Staff policies. Staff or card-network callers lacking the Customer policy will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the CardsController class and place [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] individually on Issue, Freeze, Unfreeze, and Cancel.
reasons.say: Staff and card-network payment authorisations will be rejected as forbidden because the controller requires both customer and staff permissions at once. Ask the author to move customer-only permissions onto individual endpoints.
reasons.say_facts: Staff or card-network callers lacking the Customer policy will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Class-level Customer authorization policy blocks Staff from payment authorisation
reasons.claim: CardsController is decorated with `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` at class level. In ASP.NET Core, action-level Authorize attributes are additive to class-level attributes, requiring callers of `Authorise` to satisfy both Customer and Staff policies simultaneously. Staff callers and card-network callers without Customer credentials will be denied with HTTP 403 Forbidden.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` from the controller class declaration and apply it explicitly to `Issue`, `Freeze`, `Unfreeze`, and `Cancel`, leaving `Authorise` restricted only to `Policies.Staff`.
reasons.evidence:
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class CardsController : ControllerBase
reasons.say: Payment authorisation requests from staff or card networks will fail with forbidden errors because callers are forced to hold both customer and staff roles. Verify permissions are separated per endpoint.
reasons.say_facts: Staff callers and card-network callers without Customer credentials will be denied with HTTP 403 Forbidden. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.detail: Customers gain debit card issuance and self-service freeze, unfreeze, and cancellation controls with masked card numbers in responses. Staff can authorise card payments up to a fixed 2000 limit per transaction, rounding amounts away from zero and moving authorised funds into a Suspense account.
reasons.say: Customers can now issue, freeze, unfreeze, and cancel debit cards, while staff can authorise payments up to 2,000 into suspense. Confirm these limits, rounding, and card masking match bank policy.
reasons.say_facts: This change has a high impact on customers or money: Customers gain debit card issuance and self-service freeze, unfreeze, and cancellation controls with masked card numbers in responses. Staff can authorise card payments up to a fixed 2000 limit per transaction, rounding amounts away from zero and moving authorised funds into a Suspense account. Confirm the business owner agrees.

reasons.text: Ad-hoc static in-memory account locking introduces memory leak and ineffective concurrency control
reasons.claim: CardService introduces a static unbounded ConcurrentDictionary to lock account IDs during payment authorisation. This leaks SemaphoreSlim instances permanently in memory across the process lifecycle and provides no synchronization across multi-instance deployments; ledger operations should rely on database and ledger transactional guarantees.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove AccountLocks and rely on ILedger.PostTransferAsync and database transactional/concurrency mechanisms to handle transfer concurrency.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> AccountLocks = new();
reasons.say: In-memory locking leaks memory over time and fails to prevent double-spending across multiple server instances. Ask the author to rely on database and ledger transactions instead of in-memory locks in CardService.
reasons.say_facts: This leaks SemaphoreSlim instances permanently in memory across the process lifecycle and provides no synchronization across multi-instance deployments; ledger operations should rely on database and ledger transactional guarantees. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Static AccountLocks dictionary grows indefinitely, leaking SemaphoreSlim instances
reasons.claim: AccountLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim instance for every account processed by AuthoriseAsync in a static ConcurrentDictionary without eviction or cleanup. In a long-running service processing authorisations across many customer accounts, this dictionary grows monotonically and permanently retains SemaphoreSlim objects in memory.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove in-memory static semaphore locks in favor of database/ledger concurrency controls, or utilize a bounded/evicting lock manager to prevent unbounded memory growth.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> AccountLocks = new();
reasons.say: Storing an uncleaned lock per account in CardService causes memory usage to grow endlessly, risking service crashes during busy payment periods. Ask how locks will be evicted or removed.
reasons.say_facts: In a long-running service processing authorisations across many customer accounts, this dictionary grows monotonically and permanently retains SemaphoreSlim objects in memory. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Debit card numbers generated using cryptographically weak PRNG
reasons.claim: Card numbers are sensitive financial identifiers generated using `Random.Shared`. Because `Random.Shared` is a non-cryptographic PRNG, an attacker observing generated card numbers could determine internal PRNG state and predict card numbers issued to other users.
reasons.suggested_fix: Use `System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt64(0, 1_000_000_000_000_000L)` instead of `Random.Shared` to generate unpredictable card numbers.
reasons.say: Using a predictable number generator could let attackers guess other customers' debit card numbers and steal funds. Ask the author to switch to a cryptographically secure random generator.
reasons.say_facts: Because `Random.Shared` is a non-cryptographic PRNG, an attacker observing generated card numbers could determine internal PRNG state and predict card numbers issued to other users. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: CardsController and HTTP endpoints have zero test coverage
reasons.claim: CardsController and its endpoints (Issue, Freeze, Unfreeze, Cancel, Authorise) have no test references. Route handling, status code mappings (e.g., Forbid on UnauthorizedAccessException), authorization policies (Customer vs Staff), and DTO response masking are not verified by tests.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add integration or controller tests verifying route mapping, policy enforcement (Customer and Staff policies), DTO responses, and HTTP status codes.
reasons.evidence:
[ApiController]
[Route("api/cards")]
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class CardsController : ControllerBase
reasons.say: Card HTTP endpoints have no tests, leaving routing, card-number masking, and access controls unverified for customers and staff. Ask the author to add endpoint tests covering permissions and responses.
reasons.say_facts: Route handling, status code mappings (e.g., Forbid on UnauthorizedAccessException), authorization policies (Customer vs Staff), and DTO response masking are not verified by tests. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Overly broad exception assertion in AuthoriseAsync negative amount test
reasons.claim: The test asserts ThrowsAnyAsync<Exception> instead of the specific ArgumentOutOfRangeException thrown by CardService. AuthoriseAsync. This allows any unintended failure (such as NullReferenceException or KeyNotFoundException) to pass unnoticed.
reasons.say: The negative-amount payment test accepts any error, so real bugs could slip into production unnoticed. Ask the author to assert the exact expected validation error in that test.
reasons.say_facts: This allows any unintended failure (such as NullReferenceException or KeyNotFoundException) to pass unnoticed. Decide whether it must be fixed now.
